evidence.claim: The Columbia River Gorge Scenic Byway follows SR 14 between Camas and Maryhill, with forests at its western end and rolling hills and desert country to the east.
evidence.quote: State Route 14 between Camas and Maryhill Following along the path of the Columbia River, the Columbia River Gorge Scenic Byway runs through the largest national scenic area in the U.S. Enjoy the changing landscapes as it shifts from the lush forests on the western side to the rolling hills and desert vistas of the east.

evidence.claim: State of Washington Tourism presents the byway as a 90-mile, two-hour drive through the national scenic area, with overlooks and trails along the way.
evidence.quote: Length 90 Miles | 144 KM Drive Time 2 Hours

evidence.quote: Bingen was founded by P.J. Suksdorf in 1892, and named by him for Bingen am Rhein in Germany.

evidence.claim: Sam Hill’s planned Quaker community never materialized, but his Maryhill property became home to a concrete memorial to war’s dead.
evidence.quote: Born a Quaker, Hill hoped to attract a Quaker community to eastern Washington. His plans never materialized

evidence.claim: Hill commissioned the Stonehenge replica to commemorate Klickitat County’s World War I losses.
evidence.quote: Maryhill Stonehenge, a monument to the World War I casualties of Klickitat County in the form of a Stonehenge replica

evidence.claim: He understood the ancient monument as a place of sacrifice and intended his version to express the needless sacrifice of modern warfare.
evidence.quote: Hill intended the Stonehenge replica to express that modern warfare was a form of needless human sacrifice, referencing the contemporary belief that Stonehenge was a sacrificial site.

evidence.claim: Dedicated in 1918 and completed in 1929, the memorial overlooks the Columbia Gorge.
evidence.quote: dedicated on July 4, 1918, as a memorial to the people who had died in World War I.
